solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Liqueur? Teacher sure to be tipsy draining last from bottle

indicators.note: tipsy means drunk and unsteady, so the letters of the two words before it are jumbled
draining says a letter is drawn off from the jumbled pool of letters
last from points to the final letter of the word bottle

explanation.surface: A teacher who downs the last drop from a bottle of liqueur is sure to end up tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: TEACHER and SURE together have one E too many; 'draining' removes the E at the end of 'bottle', and 'to be tipsy' mixes up the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartreuse is a green or yellow herbal liqueur made by Carthusian monks; the question mark marks it as an example.

clue.text: Search thoroughly item associated with locks

definitions.meaning: locks here are locks of hair, which a toothed grooming tool tidies

explanation.surface: Searching thoroughly for something linked to locks.
explanation.definitionFit: To comb is to search meticulously; a comb is the toothed tool used on hair, or locks.

clue.text: A clerk at first hearing about unionist, one concerned with risky calculation?

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word clerk
about says the word for hearing surrounds two pieces

parts.note: a trial is a court hearing
A is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A clerk first hears about a unionist who works out risks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' looks like part of the definition, but it supplies the A inside TRIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Actuarial work assesses insurance risk statistically, so the adjective means relating to such calculations.

clue.text: Without doubt, pitiful thing that's largely out in Holland?

definitions.text: thing that's largely out in Holland?

indicators.note: out signals that the remaining letters are set out in another order
without says a short word for doubt is taken away from pitiful

parts.note: if means a doubt, as in 'no ifs or buts'

explanation.surface: Something pitiful, truly, that is mostly blooming in the Netherlands.
explanation.walkthrough: PITIFUL less IF (doubt) leaves PITUL, which 'out' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Holland is famous for its bulb fields, where these spring flowers bloom in vast numbers.

clue.text: Impress English association ultimately favouring Anglicans

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of the word association

parts.note: for means in favour of
CE stands for the Church of England, the Anglican church

explanation.surface: The English association, in the end, impresses its support for Anglicans.
explanation.definitionFit: To impress a rule on someone is to compel it, as in pressing men into service.

clue.text: South African politicians with time probed amount in holy place

indicators.note: probed means pushed into, so the politicians and time enter the word for amount

parts.note: a sum is an amount
the ANC, African National Congress, is South Africa's governing party

explanation.surface: South African politicians, in time, investigate the amount paid into a shrine.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanctum is a sacred place, the inner part of a temple or shrine.

clue.text: Leader leaving island — Oliver?

indicators.note: leaving says one piece departs from the word for leader

parts.note: a leader is a chief

explanation.surface: Someone called Oliver steps down as leader and leaves an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Jamie Oliver is a famous British TV cook; the question mark says he is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Jamie Oliver is a celebrity cook, so he is an example of a professional cook in a kitchen.

clue.text: Magazine and books boycotting play

indicators.note: boycotting means staying away from, so the books are left out of the play

parts.note: Othello is Shakespeare's tragedy
OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: A magazine and some books boycott a play.
explanation.walkthrough: HELLO! is a British celebrity magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Hello! is a weekly celebrity news magazine published in Britain.

clue.text: One very high up a tree given warning by priest

definitions.text: One very high up a tree

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shouted warning
Father is the title of a Catholic priest

explanation.surface: Someone stuck high in a tree is warned by a priest.
explanation.walkthrough: The tree is a family tree, not a woody plant.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancestor sits near the top of a family tree, above all later generations.

clue.text: Roadside establishment essentially acceptable to most on reflection

indicators.note: on reflection says the hidden letters are read backwards
essentially means at the core, so the letters sit inside the phrase that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A wayside inn that most travellers find acceptable at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft folded 'essentially' into the definition; it is the hiding signal, since the letters lie in the essence of 'acceptable to most', and the definition is just 'Roadside establishment'.
explanation.definitionFit: A motel is a hotel for motorists, built beside main roads for overnight stops.

clue.text: Possibly unfair to include mostly select form of railway

indicators.note: to include says the jumbled letters take another piece inside them
possibly signals that the word unfair could be rearranged into other letters
mostly says the synonym of select loses its final letter

parts.note: to cull is to select or pick out from a group

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that it is unfair to include a handful of select choices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges the first word into FUNIAR, which 'to include' then splits to take in the shortened word for select.
explanation.definitionFit: A funicular is a cable railway on a steep slope, with ascending and descending cars balancing each other.

clue.text: Source of perfume enveloping last of women in passage

indicators.note: enveloping means wrapping round, so the fashion house surrounds a letter

parts.note: Chanel is the fashion house behind Chanel No 5

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word women

explanation.surface: A perfume brand wraps up the last of the women in a corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: A channel is a narrow stretch of water or a route through which things pass.

clue.text: An Irishman on fringes of normal political machine

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, giving the single letter A

indicators.note: the Irishman's name sits on the fringes of the word for normal, wrapping round it

parts.note: Pat is a stock name for an Irishman in crosswords
par means the normal level, as in 'feeling below par'

explanation.surface: An Irishman hovers on the edges of normal politics.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparat is the Soviet term for the administrative machinery of the Communist Party, hence any political organisation.

clue.text: A dessert brought back is cold

indicators.note: brought back says the dessert's name is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: a fool is a dessert of fruit purée folded into cream

explanation.surface: A pudding served again turns out to be cold.
explanation.walkthrough: A FOOL is a British pudding of crushed fruit and cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cold in manner means being distant and reserved, standing apart from others.

clue.text: Not a place cultivated around middle of grounds for fruit

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters enclose the middle letter
cultivated suggests ground worked over, so the letters are rearranged
middle of takes the central letter of the word grounds

explanation.surface: Not a place cultivated around the middle of the grounds for growing fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cultivated' rearranges NOT A PLACE, and 'around' puts the U from 'grounds' inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantaloupe is a melon with orange flesh and a ribbed rind, a type of fruit.

clue.text: Enliven number in excellent end to game

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for number inside the word for excellent

parts.note: A1, written AI in crosswords, means first-rate
checkmate ends a chess game, shortened to mate

explanation.surface: A number brought in for a fine finish livens up the match.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 means excellent; the figure 1 is taken as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To animate something is to bring it to life or make it lively, a synonym of enliven.

clue.text: Solitary note kept in a popular uprising

indicators.note: kept in says the musical note is held inside the other letters
uprising, in a down answer, means the word for popular is read upwards

parts.note: laic means lay or of the people, hence popular
so (or soh) is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A lone musical note is held back in a popular revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: Asocial describes someone who avoids company, keeping to themselves like a loner.

clue.text: Sum of money around revolutionary period in tower

indicators.note: around says the word for a sum of money surrounds the reversed period

parts.note: a mint is a large sum of money, as in 'cost a mint'

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning over, so the word for period is read backwards

parts.note: an era is a period of history

explanation.surface: Money spent during a revolution on a tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the slender tower of a mosque, from which the call to prayer is made.

clue.text: President fantastically loves to read? Not half!

indicators.note: fantastically signals that the letters are rearranged wildly
not half keeps only one half of the word read, its first two letters

explanation.surface: A president who loves to read? Absolutely!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' looks like the British exclamation meaning 'very much'; here it halves READ to RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Franklin D. and Theodore Roosevelt were both Presidents of the United States.

clue.text: Carpet felt new around much of elevated room

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters surround the shortened room
new signals that the letters of felt are made into a fresh arrangement
much of says the room's word loses its final letter

parts.note: a loft is a room up under the roof

explanation.surface: A carpet of new felt laid round most of the attic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the felt as TELF. 'Carpet' looks like a floor covering but is the British verb meaning to call someone in for a scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is to summon them for a reprimand, an informal British sense meaning to scold.

clue.text: Writer having river around sides of study

indicators.note: around says the river's name surrounds the outer letters

parts.note: the Forth is a Scottish river flowing into the Firth of Forth

indicators.note: sides of takes the first and last letters of study

explanation.surface: A writer who goes round the edges of his study by a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Frederick Forsyth was a thriller author, known for The Day of the Jackal.

clue.text: Scottish place some rule terrible (and not posh)

indicators.note: terrible signals that the letters of some rule are put into a mess
not says one letter is excluded from the pool of rearranged letters

parts.note: U stands for upper-class, a classic label meaning posh

explanation.surface: A Scottish town where some rules are terrible, though not snobbish.
explanation.walkthrough: SOME RULE has a U too many; 'not posh' removes it, and 'terrible' shuffles the rest. Melrose is a Borders town with a ruined abbey.
explanation.definitionFit: Melrose is a small town in the Scottish Borders, famous for its abbey and rugby sevens.

clue.text: Second business student overlooks it in African city

indicators.note: overlooks means sits above, which in a down answer puts the student before what follows

parts.note: mo is a moment or second, as in 'half a mo'
an MBA student studies for a Master of Business Administration
it means sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: A business student briefly overlooks something in an African city.
explanation.definitionFit: Mombasa is a major port city on the coast of Kenya.

clue.text: Stick in school a thinker

indicators.note: in says the letters lie within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A rod used in school by a thoughtful person.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathi is a heavy bamboo staff used as a weapon, especially by Indian police.

clue.text: A house in time I'm missing — and lake

indicators.note: in says the article and house go inside what remains of time
missing says the letters of I'm are taken out of time

explanation.surface: A house with time on its hands, where I'm missing, by a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Lake Tahoe lies on the California–Nevada border.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahoe is a large freshwater lake in the Sierra Nevada, on the California and Nevada border.

clue.text: Mother at home tucking into eggs and lettuce

indicators.note: tucking into means placing inside, so two pieces go into the word for eggs

parts.note: roe is the mass of eggs of a fish
ma is a familiar word for mother
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: Mum, at home, digs into eggs and salad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' suggests eating, but it means insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Romaine is the long-leaved variety of lettuce, also called cos.

clue.text: Relation favoured learning, we hear

parts.note: in means in favour, as in 'in with the boss'

indicators.note: we hear says that the next word is to be listened to rather than spelt

parts.note: lore is traditional learning or knowledge

explanation.surface: A relative favoured book learning, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone works in a non-rhotic accent, where the final R is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A relative by marriage, such as a spouse's parent, is a relation in the family.

clue.text: Authority religious follower endlessly promoted

indicators.note: promoted means moved up, so in a down answer the letters read upwards
endlessly says the follower's word loses its final letter

parts.note: a Rasta is a follower of the Rastafarian religion

explanation.surface: An authority figure, a religious follower who is constantly promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts RASTA to RAST, and 'promoted' turns that upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsar is used for a powerful official or expert put in charge, like a 'drugs tsar'.

clue.text: A ceremonial burning's involved in this neglected heap usually (not American)

definitions.text: A ceremonial burning's involved in this

indicators.note: neglected suggests something left in disorder, so the letters are scrambled
not says letters are dropped from the jumbled pool

explanation.surface: A bonfire is part of this ritual: an untended heap, normally.
explanation.walkthrough: HEAP USUALLY with US removed, by 'not American', leaves nine letters that 'neglected' rearranges. Up Helly Aa is a Viking fire festival in Lerwick, Shetland, where a longship is burnt.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shetland festival climaxes with torchbearers setting fire to a replica Viking galley.

clue.text: English city? Get day in the worst parts

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation for day goes inside the dregs

parts.note: lees are the dregs, the worst part left at the bottom

explanation.surface: An English city where a day spent in the worst areas is the question.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds is a large city in West Yorkshire, an example of an English city.

clue.text: Uniform shown by Eastern archdeacon

parts.note: Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: A uniform worn by an archdeacon from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniform as an adjective means consistent or unvarying, the same sense as level and regular.

clue.text: Tar was here unsettling seabird

indicators.note: unsettling signals that the letters of the three words are disturbed

explanation.surface: A sailor was here, upsetting a seabird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tar' is a sailor in the surface but only fodder here.
explanation.definitionFit: Shearwaters are long-winged ocean birds that skim low over the waves.
